title: Changing verbs
description: Verbs that change their ending in the present.
grammarNote: Many verbs change their stem in the present: querer becomes quiero, dormir becomes duermo.

explanation.summary: About thirty Spanish verbs change their stem in the present instead of changing their ending. The change is only in the stressed vowel, and it never happens in the nosotros and vosotros forms.

sections.heading: Three kinds of change
sections.body: E becomes ie: querer, querer to quiere, dormir to duerme. O becomes ue: poder to puede, volver to vuelve. And E becomes i: pedir to pide, seguir to sigue. The nosotros and vosotros forms keep the original stem:queremos, dormimos, pedimos.

sections.heading: The yo form is often the odd one
sections.body: The three changes only apply to the stressed vowel, and in the yo form that vowel is the one before the ending. Some verbs also change the ending in the yo form: dormir becomes duermo, not duemo. And a few verbs change everywhere except the nosotros form: querer is quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren.

items.note: The e changes to ie: quiero, quieres, quiere.
The o changes to ue: puedo, puedes, puede.
The o changes to ue: duermo, duermes, duerme.
The e changes to i: sigo, sigues, sigue.
The e changes to ie: prefiero, prefieres, prefiere.
The e changes to ie: miento, mientes, miente.
The e changes to ie: cierro, cierras, cierra.
The e changes to ie: despierto, despiertas, despierta.
The e changes to ie: siento, sientes, siente.

drills.note: Dormir also changes the ending in the yo form.
Pedir changes e to i and drops the e.
The nosotros form keeps the original stem.
